quest.title: A Dry Well Doth Not Reflect the Stars
quest.description: Following the hints in the dictionary, you and Paimon decide to deliver the assignment to Mona. It should be a simple task... or so it seems.
quest.rewards_formatted: Hero's Wit x3, Guide to Resistance x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mona! We have something for you!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! You're full of energy today.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You have something for me, you said? Is it... some quick and easy way to make Mora, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, actually, it's some kind of "task" from your master.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's a hard no! Ugh, but I guess I don't have a choice, huh... An enterprising spirit is important, and all that.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I just know it's going to be torture, though. I know that old hag all too well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why don't you just take a look first?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh, this book... doesn't seem so special to me.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Whoa! Letters just fell out of it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Maybe she's trying to... reconcile with you?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: No idea. Either way, it looks like I'm supposed to open these three letters in order. Well, let's start with the first one.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: If this is her "task," it should be okay for us all to read. C'mon, let's see what this is about.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Oh, how long it's been, my student. I'm afraid to report that getting up and about is becoming harder and harder these days..."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Heh, the sympathy card. She could've tried to make it sound a bit more genuine, at least...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Remember when I would chase you, and you would run for dear life, trying to use that Hydro phantom of yours to distract me? Ah, seems like it was just yesterday..."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Now, you're off on your own, and I laze the days away in my rocking chair. I really should get some exercise again..."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, then get it some other way, you old hag!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Um, on second thought, this seems kinda private...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Now, I'm sure you're curious as to the purpose of this letter. And to that, I say this... If you want to learn how to predict the fate of an entire kingdom, or even the entire world..."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Head to Sumeru and search for the gate to an underground kingdom. Once there, open the second letter."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh, but she knows how to lure people in, that's for sure. Is she serious about passing on her secret technique?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Guess she really is getting old.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You two have such a weird dynamic. When you talk about sentimental stuff... you fight. But when it comes to dry, academic stuff, you get all emotional...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, this "gate to an underground" kingdom sounds familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Wait, you've heard of it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. It should be the same one we're thinking of.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Perfect! I don't even need to investigate, then! That means no hired guide, no lodging, no shelling out Mora left and right!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: C'mon, there's no time to waste. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And since you didn't mention a transportation fee just now, Paimon's guessing that means...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yep! Same method as usual! Let's go!

talks.objective: Head to the gates of Khaenri'ah
Head to the gates of Khaenri'ah

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, this brings back memories of summertime. It's actually kinda refreshing!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: So, this is the gate to the ancient kingdom of Khaenri'ah...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I'm sure a lot of secrets and tragedies lie behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, let's open the second letter!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Let me see here... Yep. It's this one.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "As the ancient Sumeru saying goes: Rote knowledge bears no fruit, until it is watered with the showers of wisdom. With that in mind, there is a phenomenon in this land known as the 'Sign of Apaosha.'"

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "It is a celestial mark that burns in response to an all-too-ardent desire for the truth. In that sense, perhaps it's more fitting to call it a 'Sign of Truth' instead..."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: The records of this ancient kingdom state there are several large subterranean lakes in Khaenri'ah, clear and calm as mirrors, whose surfaces reflect the true stars.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "This is because the 'Sign of Truth' created in the water is able to bypass the false sky and connect to the outer universe."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I had no idea!

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "To observe the gravitational forces and influence of celestial bodies, one must be able to see past the false sky. Only by obtaining these cosmic parameters can one predict the fate of this world."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Now, my task for you is as follows: Open a 'Sign of Truth' in front of the gate to Khaenri'ah."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The rest is a bunch of stuff about the ceremony the old hag came up with to summon this thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, all these planetary trajectories and... runes... Paimon's not even gonna try to make sense of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do you say, Mona? Are you gonna attempt it?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, I hate to admit it, but it looks like the parameters she came up with could work.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Frankly, this prospect is quite exciting — and heading back now will just cost me another night of lodging. So... no better time than the present!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Emissaries of the enduring stars, wanderers over ecliptic and equatorial planes, radiant celestial brethren...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Traverse the twisted paths of the cavernous void. I, Mona Megistus, the Astrologist, invoke the power of Hydro to balance the scales.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: By wisdom and truth, let the thirst be relieved. I, Mona Megistus, the Astrologist, summon you, O stars, to stand before me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Did it work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaah! Monsters? How did that happen?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: No dice. The Sign of Truth only opened long enough for the monsters to slip through.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Darn it! I didn't get a glimpse of the real stars at all. Whatever... I'll just take it out on you.

talks.objective: Head to the gates of Khaenri'ah

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, that's that...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, the old hag said to open the third letter once it was all said and done.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But, I couldn't make it work. So... should I still open it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Y'know, Paimon thinks she understands your dynamic a lot better now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, she didn't say you had to *successfully* complete the ceremony, so you can open it. It'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh, I guess. All the same, I doubt she has anything nice to say.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "If you're reading this, it means you attempted to open the Sign of Truth."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "...Hahahaha. Seriously? I can't believe you actually tried it!"

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What are you laughing at, you old hag!?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Khaenri'ah was home to several lakes of stars, rendering the fabric of space in that area comparatively unstable. As a result, attempts to break through the firmament through non-physical means were more likely to succeed."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "In any case, I knew this place was well-hidden and wouldn't be frequented by too many people. As such, any negative effects of failing to open the Sign of Truth would remain small-scale."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "And of course, as my student, I felt sure you would have the chops to deal with the Abyssal creatures that roam beyond the false sky."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Even if you couldn't beat them, I am certain you could out-run them. You always were fast on your feet."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "Ah, connecting hydromancy to the kind of wisdom that quenches 'thirst'... Truly, my genius knows no bounds."

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: "The practical application of the Scryglass has also reduced disturbances caused by the false sky. Hah, I'd like to see Alice try and top that!"

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Mona cuts it off there — apparently, the old hag proceeds to brag for a further few thousand words.\n\nAfter sorting through the observation results, you all return to Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The ceremony failed, but the old hag's new theory seems workable.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I have a better grasp of hydromancy now... and the perfect test subjects to test it on.
